pattern: archaeologists dug at Wachesaw and found|digs at Wachesaw found
struck: Before anyone built here, archaeologists dug at Wachesaw and found more than half a million artifacts.
use: A University of South Carolina study of Wachesaw and the neighboring Richmond Hill plantation found more than half a million artifacts [Michie, quoted in the Horry Independent].

struck: Dinner is at Kimbels, on the bluff above the waterway.
use: Kimbels, the club's formal restaurant, is on the bluff above the waterway and the 18th green.

pattern: takes public tee times|(?:is|are) open to the public[^.]{0,40}Wachesaw East|Wachesaw East[^.]{0,60}open to the public
struck: The course takes public tee times, so you share it with visitors.
use: Tee times are booked online on the club's site, and SC Golf lists the course as semi-private.

pattern: one of McConnell's 17 clubs|members can play the other McConnell
struck: It is one of McConnell's 17 clubs, and members can play the other McConnell clubs.
use: McConnell Golf lists 17 properties in four states, and Reserve members get reciprocal privileges at its sister clubs [club site].

struck: A golf membership covers the family's dining and social events.
use: A golf membership includes access to the club's dining and social events, for the member's family and dependents up to age 25 [club site].

struck: a private Greg Norman course of 7,200 yards, cut through the woods and around the marsh.
use: a private Greg Norman course of up to 7,200 yards, laid out through 160 acres of natural wetlands [club site; course architect's site].

pattern: Coast Guard (?:calls|designates|names) it|Coast Guard calls it a hurricane hole
struck: the U.S. Coast Guard calls it a hurricane hole.
use: the S.C. Clean Marina Program describes it as designated a Hurricane Hole by the U.S. Coast Guard [SC Clean Marina Program, 2024].

struck: six markers along it tell that history hole by hole.
use: five markers along it tell that history, at the 4th, 5th and 8th holes, near the 9th green and on the way to the 1st tee [course operator's site].

pattern: cemetery of enslaved people, with 38 graves|containing 38 graves
struck: By the 8th hole is the Oatland cemetery of enslaved people, with 38 graves, protected inside the community.
use: By the 8th hole is the Oatland cemetery of enslaved people, which the community counts at 38 graves [Litchfield by the Sea].

struck: One car barcode opens both gates on the way to Litchfield by the Sea's beach.
use: One vehicle barcode is issued for the owner's gated community and for Litchfield by the Sea access [Litchfield by the Sea].

pattern: bought the land in 1926 for|bought the three plantations for duck
struck: a Pennsylvania businessman bought the land in 1926 for duck and quail hunting.
use: in 1926 a Pennsylvania businessman bought the three tracts, which were used for duck and quail hunting [Chicora Foundation, RS11].

pattern: golf course crosses the land of three|course across three rice plantations|crosses the land of three rice plantations
struck: Willbrook's golf course crosses the land of three rice plantations, Willbrook, Oatland and Turkey Hill.
use: Willbrook was built on the land of three rice plantations, Willbrook, Oatland and Turkey Hill [Chicora, RS11], and the course winds through a pair of them [course site].

pattern: water (?:is )?on 15 of (?:the course's )?18 holes, most of it
struck: Water is on 15 of the course's 18 holes, most of it along the edges.
use: There is water on 15 of 18 holes, often on the edge of the layout [course site].

struck: Willbrook was part of a 24,000-acre grant made by the Lords Proprietors to Robert Daniel in 1711.
use: A 2,400-acre tract was granted to Robert Daniel in 1711, of which 1,490 acres lay on Waccamaw Neck [Chicora Foundation, RS11, PDF p. 48]. (Publish no acreage if the page does not need it. The old struck pattern for 2,400 is itself wrong.)
